To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) noise in the levels of a key regulator can lead to the existence of multiple steady states in a cell, and (ii) this noise can lead to the emergence of different behaviors in the same population of cells.
the noise in the expression of stress response genes is not a random process but is rather the result of a complex interplay between the cell's regulatory network and the environment.
Noise in the levels of a key stress response regulator is amplified in response to environmental stress, but the magnitude of the response is cell-to-cell variable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of biological noise in the context of the stress response of bacteria.
the analysis of the role of noise in the behavior of cells, with the aim of providing a better understanding of the stochastic processes that underlie the behavior of biological systems.
the analysis of stochasticity in biological systems, and in particular in bacterial chemotaxis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
noise and heterogeneity are two sides of the same coin, and that they are tightly related to each other (Huang, in press).
the noise in the biological world is a consequence of the stochasticity that characterizes the physical world.
noise is a ubiquitous phenomenon in biological systems, which is not always detrimental, but can be used by nature to generate heterogeneity in the cellular population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
noise is an important factor to be taken into account for the design of synthetic gene circuits.
the noise is not only a nuisance but also a source of biological information, which is used by cells to make decisions and to adapt to environmental changes (Becskei and Stelling, 2008).
we are interested in understanding how noise affects biological systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of noise, the direction of the gradient is defined by the average of a large number of noisy measurements.
the same stochastic process that is used by cells to get a sense for the direction of a gradient can be used by cells to sense a change in the environment.
the noise of a system can be used to infer the existence of multiple attractors and to determine the direction in which a system will move.
